entries.title: Morgan Park showcases its aerial attack in Payton win
entries.summary: <p>Morgan Park opened the season with challenging road trips to Downers Grove North and Edwardsville and a matchup with Notre Dame. The Mustangs emerged with two wins and a five-point, resume-building loss to ranked Downers North.</p><p>For coach Chris James, the challenge now is keeping his team’s level high in Public League play.</p><p>“I’m not as worried about it as I used to be,” James said. “We do a lot now, as much as we can, to prohibit anything slipping. We used to play bad against teams we should beat, but we are getting better at that.”</p><p>Morgan Park knocked off Payton 61-7 on <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/high-school-football/scores/2026/09/10/high-school-football-scores-chicago-illinois" >Saturday</a> at Stagg Stadium.</p><p>The Mustangs ran the ball well over the first three weeks of the season so the focus against Payton was on junior quarterback Ronald Smith Jr. throwing the ball.</p><p>It was a success. Smith was 10-for-13 passing for 221 yards with three touchdowns and one interception.</p><p>He connected with Jeremiah Harvey for a 42-yard TD, Travezz Jones for a 33-yard TD, and Mark Dossous Jr. on an 11-yard score. Jones had four catches for 94 yards.</p><p>“I’m feeling good,” Smith said. “We have been progressing every week. We made a few mistakes the first week and then got better. We still have to improve, though.”</p><p>Senior running back William Smith Jr. opened the scoring with a 72-yard TD run, and Kenneth Sims ripped off a 57-yard TD run in the third quarter.</p><p>Linebacker Raymond Gilbert junior led the defensive effort for Morgan Park (3-1, 1-0 Red Star) with a couple of sacks and a fumble recovery.</p><p>Payton turned the ball over seven times. There were multiple fumbles and several special teams mistakes.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item" data-crop=""> <figure class="Figure"><a class="AnchorLink" entries.title: Chief Keef Live 2026 Tour concert in Chicago postponed
entries.summary: <p>Saturday was supposed to be a landmark day for Chief Keef fans. </p><p>Fans from Chicago and beyond arrived at Huntington Bank Pavilion at Northerly Island in their best outfits to see the rapper's first show within the city limits in more than a decade.</p><p>As massive groups of spectators lined up in front of the entrance for the Chief Keef Live 2026 Tour kickoff concert, the venue posted a message on its <a class="Link" href="https://www.instagram.com/p/DdNISDVj9JS/" target="_blank" >Instagram account</a> around 6 p.m. that the show was delayed. About an hour later, another message appeared saying Keef would not be performing at all. </p><p>"Chief Keef’s September 12th performance at Huntington Bank Pavilion has been postponed," the post read. "All previously purchased tickets will be honored for the new date."</p><p>Neither the venue nor Keef representatives provided a reason for the cancellation. </p><p><i>This is a developing story. Check back with Sun-Times.com for updates. </i> </p>
entries.author: Mark Braboy

entries.title: Will Venable ready to adjust as needed as White Sox try to shake late-season funk
entries.summary: <p>ST. LOUIS, Mo. – With losses in nine of their last 12 games and their division lead shaved down to the bone, the announcement of Saturday’s White Sox lineup seemed to reveal the kind of major shake-up for which the offense’s September struggles had been calling.</p><p>Colson Montgomery and Braden Montgomery–both entering Saturday with an OPS under .600 for the month–were shifted to the bottom two spots of the order. Kyle Teel, <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox/2026/09/10/slowed-by-injury-white-sox-catcher-kyle-teel-still-has-tools-for-a-breakout-will-venable-ryan-fuller-bat-speed-chris-getz" target="_blank" ><u>projected preseason to be a middle of the order fixture</u></a> but easing back from an ankle injury, was moved up to second.</p><p>Instead, manager Will Venable defused such notions of a big, reactive change.</p><p>"The change in lineup is not about performance or anything,” Venable said.</p><p>Near the end of Year 2 of the White Sox under Venable’s stewardship, it’s imprudent to assume he’s trying to send a message through the lineup when platoon matchups are the more likely explanation. Sure enough, his expectation that the Cardinals were planning to piggyback right-handed starter Kyle Leahy with left-hander Cooper Hjerpe drove a strategy geared around left-handed bats at the top of the order.</p><p>Of course, with the White Sox fighting for their playoff lives, there’s a world where this order has some staying power.</p><p>“Maybe we score a bunch of runs and we want to keep it exactly the same,” Venable quipped.</p><p>But is there a major adjustment coming as the White Sox suffer through their worst baseball of the season at a decidedly inopportune time? The window for a proactive response to the second half fades of Montgomery, Munetaka Murakami, even spitfire rookie leadoff man Sam Antonacci, has closed. Caleb Bonemer and his 37 minor league home runs could be an intriguing option next year, but there’s no late-season offensive impact waiting for the call in Triple-A Charlotte.</p><p>“We played together all year, the vibes aren’t down,” said Chase Meidroth. “We have to move forward and find a way to win.”</p><p>Hitting coach Derek Shomon is grinding through adjustments in the batting cage, but from a deployment perspective, there’s not many transformative options. Instead Venable has largely kept the faith with his existing core, and his players echo the same steady confidence. What this Sox roster lacks in postseason experience, they make up for in experience in absorbing losses and trusting things will get better.</p><p>“There's been parts of the season where we weren't pitching well, we weren't hitting well, we weren't doing this or we weren't doing that,” Davis Martin told the Sun-Times. “We came out of it every time.”</p><p>“We know things are going to pass and we are going to get back on track when we need to,” said Colson Montgomery.</p><p>The question obviously also extends to the pitching staff, especially where using Sean Newcomb as an opener in front of him did little to stanch <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox/2026/09/11/white-sox-starter-luis-castillo-feels-hes-very-very-close-to-righting-ship-after-working-on-mechanics-colson-montgomery-strikeout-record-chase-meidroth-joey-bart-will-venable" target="_blank" ><u>the bleeding from trade deadline acquisition Luis Castillo</u></a>. Newcomb, <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox/2026/08/31/white-sox-sean-newcomb-starter-or-reliever-bullpen-will-venable-grant-taylor-sean-burke-free-agency-chris-getz-rotation-relief" target="_blank" ><u>the heavily-used rock of the bullpen all year long</u></a>, has now been charged with runs in four-straight outings, even though Saturday night was a case of Castillo allowing an inherited run to score, as the right-hander saw his velocity drop into the low-90s, was pulled after less than three innings of work and now has a 7.76 ERA in a White Sox uniform</p><p>The Sox do have starting pitching options in the minors that could be worth exploring, and that could begin as soon as Sunday. Venable contends that if anything, he’s ready to respond to how his players are performing in the moment more than ever.</p><p>“If we’re in early-April, May baseball, you’re kind of spreading out the love, spreading out the opportunity to make sure guys are plugged in,” Venable said. “Now it’s just about one day, and today, and how you’re going to win that game.”</p><p>During this skid, Venable has spent some postgame sessions lamenting moves that haven’t worked out, but insists he’s not hesitant to pull the trigger on some new ones going forward.</p><p>“If there's adjustments that are necessary,” Venable said, “We're going to make them.”<br></p>
entries.author: James Fegan

entries.title: Westinghouse cruises past Curie
entries.summary: <p>Westinghouse missed the IHSA playoffs last year and were dropped from the Public League's top Red division to the second tier this season.</p><p>Neither development sat well with the Warriors, who are aiming to reestablish themselves as an upper-level team in the city.</p><p>"It definitely put a little chip on our shoulder for sure," junior two-way standout Ethan Wiley said.</p><p>Saturday's 42-6 romp past Curie at Rockne Stadium was a step in the right direction.</p><p>Senior Jaidyn Gandy ran nine times for 132 yards — all in the first half — including touchdowns of one and 50 yards. Wiley had five carries for 35 yards and a score. Bernard Mitchell Jr. also had a 50-yard touchdown run.</p><p>Gandy, who also runs track, moved from receiver to running back this season.</p><p>"He's been getting better every week, just working, learning different things," Westinghouse coach Julius Carter said.</p><p>"I love it," Gandy said of the switch. "Just anything to help the team. I know Coach is going to put me in the best possible position to succeed, and I just trust in that."</p><p>He does have previous experience at running back, so the position is not completely foreign to him.</p><p>"We've just got to be a football player at the end of the day," Gandy said.</p><p>Meanwhile, Carter said, "Ethan Wiley is probably one of the best players in the Public League. He's underrated, most definitely."</p><p>Wiley made the All-City team as a sophomore last year.</p><p>"He's a receiver, DB, whatever we need him at," Carter said. "He can do it all — run the ball, he's all-around, just an athlete."</p><p>"I definitely feel like I've got a lot to prove because there's a lot of guys out here [who are] getting way more exposed," Wiley said. "And I know I'm better than them. So yeah, I feel like it's a lot to prove out here."</p><p>Though they're still a win shy of their 2025 total, the Warriors (3-1, 1-0) are IHSA playoff-eligible this season under the expanded postseason format. But they still have a lot to play for in the regular season, even as they are missing some key players who are hurt.</p><p>"We still want to finish strong," Carter said. "The goal was to win conference, make the city and state playoffs and just keep things going in the right direction. So even with the injuries, that's the goal."</p><p>Curie (2-2, 0-1), which was shut out by Lincoln Park last week, also is navigating some injury issues. On Saturday, turnovers were a problem and led to three of Westinghouse's seven touchdowns.</p><p>One bright spot for the Condors was freshman backup quarterback Treyveon Townsend, who had six carries for 33 yards and a TD.</p><p>"I knew these were going to be two tests for us, just being that they were in the [top Red] conference last year," Curie coach Jarve Lewis-Bey said. "But I wasn't expecting this.</p><p>"We knew what they were going to do. They ran the same plays the last three weeks, they ran them this week. We still couldn't stop them."</p>

entries.title: White Sox get needed boost in dramatic game-winning home run from Randal Grichuk
entries.summary: <p>ST. LOUIS – Throughout losing nine of 12 games, matching a season-high four-game skid, and seeing their division lead over the Cleveland Guardians shrink to just half a game, White Sox players and coaches insisted that vibes remained high.</p><p><a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox/2026/09/12/will-venable-ready-to-adjust-as-needed-as-white-sox-try-to-shake-late-season-funk-colson-montgomery-davis-martin-chase-meidroth-luis-castillo-sean-newcomb" target="_blank" ><u>They professed faith in the brand of baseball</u></a>, the slugging-reliant offense, the piecemeal pitching staff and the loose clubhouse atmosphere that carried them to this point, would pull them out of a mid-September dive before they crashed into the ground. Then 35-year-old Randal Grichuk improbably sprayed a two-out, two-strike, two-run go-ahead opposite-field homer over the right field wall of Busch Stadium, where he began his career 12 years prior.</p><p>After Bryan Hudson pitched a perfect ninth to complete a theft of a 6-5 victory, something akin to all the injuries of a hockey team being revealed after a long postseason run played out in the visitor’s locker room, but in the form of White Sox players admitting how much they needed the moment that Grichuk provided.</p><p>“It was something that we really needed,” said Grichuk. “Hopefully now we can keep playing our game, and be in a lot better place.”</p><p>"I think it can do a lot,” said manager Will Venable of the win.</p><p>It was left unspoken, but it helps that the Guardians lost earlier in the afternoon in Minneapolis, and the White Sox are 1 ½ games up again, and will land in Cleveland on Sunday night still in possession of the American League Central lead.</p><p>“Momentum is a powerful thing,” said Kyle Teel, who came back from an 0-2 count against Cardinals closer Riley O’Brien to walk in front of Grichuk.</p><p>A momentum shift would be good, since the Sox certainly didn’t receive any assurances that all is in working order on Saturday in St. Louis. The 28-man roster is surely not that consumed with <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox/2026/09/12/white-sox-amateur-scouting-director-mike-shirley-resigns-chris-getz-garrett-crochet-colson-montgomery-grant-taylor-jacob-gonzalez-hagen-smith-caleb-bonemer" target="_blank" ><u>the club’s amateur scouting director resigning while under internal investigation</u></a>, but the more pressing issue of <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox/2026/09/11/white-sox-starter-luis-castillo-feels-hes-very-very-close-to-righting-ship-after-working-on-mechanics-colson-montgomery-strikeout-record-chase-meidroth-joey-bart-will-venable" target="_blank" ><u>trade deadline acquisition Luis Castillo’s struggles</u></a> got worse, if anything.</p><p>Pitching behind an opener, Castillo lasted just 2 ⅔ innings and yielded three runs. The damage could have been worse had he not snuck a fastball by Cardinals RBI leader Alec Burleson with the bases loaded to end the fourth; a feat nearly as miraculous as Grichuk’s blast given that Castillo’s velocity had flagged into the low-90s, with no easy answers as to why.</p><p>“I don’t know why because I felt that my mechanics were good, my body feels good,” Castillo said via interpreter.</p><p>It’s a bit late for another skipped start to work further on his delivery.</p><p>“I don't know if we have time to do that again,” said Venable. “The No. 1 thing is to make sure that he's healthy.”</p><p>Venable appeared to shake up his lineup on Saturday, sliding a resurgent Teel near the top of the order, and moving the struggling Colson Montgomery and Braden Montgomery down. But he insisted he was just playing matchups for handedness as always, and not making a reactive late-season switch.</p><p>After second-guessing his own deployment of pinch-hitters in recent days, he was once more back to his aggressive ways, calling Grichuk off the bench to face a lefty in the top of the fourth.</p><p>When it meant that Grichuk wound up in a right-right matchup with O’Brien with two outs in the ninth, another constantly preached element of White Sox baseball emerged: stay on the fastball, even after four-straight sliders put him behind in the count 1-2.</p><p>"He took advantage of a mistake,” Venable said. “We all thought that there was another offspeed coming down below the zone.”</p><p>Sometimes an opponent’s mistake can be the difference, and the Sox were bound–they insisted–to get one eventually.</p><p>“Luckily he left a sinker on over [the plate],” Grichuk said. “Haven’t been able to get that big hit to push us over the top and I know we all feel it. Luckily tonight I was able to come through.”</p>
entries.author: James Fegan

entries.title: Police investigate death of woman pulled from Lake Michigan
entries.summary: <p>Chicago police are investigating the death of a woman who was pulled from Lake Michigan on Friday.</p><p>The unidentified woman was pronounced dead after her body was recovered from the water about 8 p.m. near the 300 block of South DuSable Lake Shore Drive, police said.</p><p>Area 3 detectives are conducting an investigation, pending autopsy results, police said. </p><p>No further information was available.</p>
entries.author: Sun-Times Wire

entries.title: Woman, 2 teens wounded in Chicago Lawn shooting
entries.summary: <p>A woman and two teenagers were wounded in a shooting Saturday night in Chicago Lawn, according to Chicago police.</p><p>A 37-year-old woman, a 17-year-old girl, and a 15-year-old boy were standing outside along the 7100 block of South Campbell Avenue at about 6:58 p.m. when two men fired multiple gunshots at them. </p><p>The adult woman suffered gunshot wounds to her head, right hand, and left wrist, police said. </p><p>She was taken to Advocate Christ Medical Center in critical condition, according to police. </p><p>The 15-year-old boy suffered a gunshot wound to his neck and a graze wound to his chest, police said. </p><p>He was taken to Comer Children’s Hospital in good condition. </p><p>The 17-year-old girl suffered a gunshot wound to her right knee and was taken to the University of Chicago Medical Center in good condition, according to police.</p><p>The unidentified shooters were last seen in a light-colored sedan, police said.</p><p>Area 1 detectives are investigating.</p>
entries.author: Sun-Times Wire

entries.title: Police investigate death of 1-year-old girl in West Ridge
entries.summary: <p>Chicago police are investigating the death of a 1-year-old girl who was found wounded and unresponsive in West Ridge on Saturday morning, police said.</p><p>The unidentified child was found with visible injuries to her lower body at about 11:40 a.m. along the 2600 block of West Rosemont Avenue, according to police.</p><p>She was taken to Saint Francis Hospital in critical condition, where she died, police said.</p><p>Area 3 detectives are investigating the death, police said. An official cause of death has not been determined. <br></p>
